title: January 2027 Warm-Weather Trip Options
missingWindowNote: The Worldwide ranking was priced for Jan 5–12 only. The Sheet has no Jan 2–9 fares for this ranking.
paymentNote: Pay with Chase Sapphire Preferred (no foreign transaction fee). Points estimates come from Credit Max and are unverified.
notes: Totals are for 2 people and 7 nights: one LAX round trip plus one DTW round trip. For drive trips, she flies DTW–LAX and they drive the HR-V from Hawthorne.
howToRead: Checked Wed Nov 11, 2026 (PT). Fares are live Google Flights round trips for Jan 5-12, 2027: one from LAX and one from DTW, economy, using a reasonable option rather than the absolute cheapest 30h+ itinerary. HIGH adds $300 for standard economy or bags. Lodging comes from Airbnb entire-place searches for Jan 5-12 (25th-75th percentile of the first page) plus estimated taxes. Transport, food and activities are ESTIMATES. For drive trips, she flies DTW-LAX and they drive the HR-V from Hawthorne (gas at $4.19/gal, 30 mpg). Long-haul time cost: Europe means losing about 1 day each way and a 5-9h time shift; Hong Kong and Taiwan mean losing about 1.5-2 days and a 15-16h shift for him. Points figures are Credit Max's estimates (1 cent per point, award space not checked) and did not affect any ranking. Use the Sapphire Preferred for travel and abroad, never the Freedom card abroad.
asOfDetail: Wed Nov 11, 2026 (Pacific Time). All prices are snapshots and change daily. Nothing was booked or held.

method.detail: https://github.com/skywain/trip-planner-skill. Used its hard rules: prices and hours come from tools, never memory; every price carries a source and as-of date; a missing price is flagged, not guessed; cheap keyless data first (it recommends the fast-flights Google Flights scanner, which is the same data source used here); never book or pay.

https://github.com/mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills/blob/main/skills/trip-planner/SKILL.md. Used its output shape: day-by-day plan grouped by area with slack, book-ahead flags, a budget range split into lodging / food / activities / transit with the big swing factors named, and 'verify locally' notes for closures and safety.

https://github.com/ZawYePhyo/travel-planner-skill. Used its criteria: optimize around pace, season, food and logistics; research unstable facts live (ticket prices, transport, reservation pressure); separate free stops, paid core stops and optional paid upgrades.

1) Took Head Honcho's 7 candidates plus the Costa Rica honorable mention. 2) Re-pulled every flight live from Google Flights for both date windows. 3) Pulled Airbnb lodging prices for Jan 5-12. 4) Pulled climate normals (NOAA / Mexico SMN / WMO / Costa Rica IMN) plus ERA5 rain frequency. 5) Checked advisories, park fees, Hawaii tax and Kilauea status. 6) Scored each option on hiking/outdoors, food, museums, warmth, logistics and cost, then ranked. 7) Ran a separate skeptical QA pass (below) and recomputed.
Jalisco is US State Dept Level 3 'Reconsider travel' (advisory dated May 29, 2026). The earlier research didn't flag this. Oaxaca, Mexico City and Baja California Sur are Level 2.

method.item: 2. Hawaii cost range lowered and tax corrected
method.detail: Hawaii lodging tax is 18.712%, not 18.5% (state TAT rose to 11% on Jan 1, 2026, plus 3% county TAT and 4.712% max GET pass-on). Airbnb whole-unit rentals for Jan 5-12 came in at about $1.35k-1.9k per week incl. tax on the Big Island ($1.85k-2.4k Kihei, Maui), below the $300-500/night hotel assumption. Big Island total is now $3.8k-6.1k for Jan 5-12 (was $4.6k-7.6k). Resort hotels would push it back toward the old range.

method.item: 3. Hawaii Jan 2-9 flights are higher than reported
method.detail: KOA cheapest is $1,256 for two on Jan 2-9 (vs $894 on Jan 5-12). OGG is $1,034 / $894. The earlier $870-1,074 range only holds for Maui or the later window.

Oaxaca $1,948 (Jan 2-9) / $1,102 (Jan 5-12): confirmed. Mexico City $742 (Jan 5-12): confirmed (connecting; the nonstop is $974). La Paz $1,068 (Jan 2-9, 1 stop): confirmed, and the Jan 5-12 nonstop is $914. Puerto Vallarta nonstop $962 (Jan 5-12): confirmed, but Jan 2-9 is $1,244.
Cheapest fares may be basic economy. A spot check of non-basic fares for Jan 2-9 found +$24 (KOA), +$290 (OGG), +$328 (OAX) for two, so the HIGH totals add $300.

The first weather pull used ERA5 gridded reanalysis (Open-Meteo), which ran too cool for inland valleys (Oaxaca 77F vs the official 84F; Palm Springs 64F vs NOAA's 71F). Switched the Ranking to official station normals. ERA5 is used only for the share of rainy days. Oaxaca 84/51F and Mexico City 72/47F both held up.
Joshua Tree (Twentynine Palms) normals are 63/42F and Tucson 67/41F, so both rank below the warm-weather flights. Their cost ranges tightened to $2.2k-3.3k (JT+PS) and $1.7k-2.7k (Tucson).

method.item: 8. Big Island chosen over Maui as the Hawaii pick; Maui kept as an alternative
method.detail: Kilauea is in an ongoing episodic eruption (episode 56 ended Nov 5, 2026, alert level ADVISORY). Combined with Kona snorkeling and more varied hikes, and lower lodging costs, that puts the Big Island ahead. Some park areas are closed for hazards and construction.

method.item: 9. Costa Rica stays an honorable mention
method.detail: Jan 5-12 cheapest fare is 3 stops (about 10.5h). The nonstop was only found for Jan 2-9 at $1,872 for two.
Oaxaca $2.4k-3.9k (Jan 5-12) / $3.2k-4.8k (Jan 2-9); La Paz + Todos Santos $2.9k-4.8k; Mexico City $2.3k-4.0k; Puerto Vallarta $3.0k-5.1k.

Food, activities, car rental totals, transfers, and the Mexico/CA/AZ/CR lodging tax multipliers are estimates by the planner, labeled as such and dated Nov 11, 2026. Drive distances and times are approximate.

method.item: 1. Switched from cheapest fares to realistic ones
method.detail: Several of the cheapest fares were 2-stop itineraries taking 20-33h each way (Cartagena $964, Rio $2,332, Santiago $2,364). The totals use the cheapest 1-stop or nonstop fare instead; the cheapest any-stop fare is shown in its own column.
Official normals put Cusco at 69/46F with about 20 rain days in January, and Machu Picchu gets about 341 mm. It's the wrong season for a warm-weather trip, so it's listed but not ranked.
The State Dept rated Colombia Level 3 'Reconsider travel' on Mar 31, 2026. Both Colombian options moved down even though Cartagena is the cheapest.
US$80.90 per person, via VFS Global only (gov.br, updated Oct 29, 2026). Added $162 to Rio.
IDEAM normals are 82/64F, spring-like. Its verdict is set against Oaxaca, which is warmer and cheaper.
No South American option beats or ties the current top 5 for a 7-night trip. The best one, Buenos Aires + Mendoza, would slot around #6.

The Ranking tab had listed it for Mexico City. It has been closed since Aug 10, 2025, with no reopening date. Replaced with La Malinche (7.9 mi, 4,320 ft, AllTrails; may have snow Dec-Mar) and Ajusco / Pico del Aguila (3.1 mi, 2,349 ft).

The new test is highs about 55F+, lows above freezing, not rain-soaked. Kyoto (48/35F), Osaka (49/37F) and Fukuoka (50/39F) fail. Bali (about 19 rain days) and Cairns (about 16) are in wet season. Mexico City, Tucson and Joshua Tree no longer get a 'not warm' penalty. Granada (34F lows) is borderline and is noted.

method.item: 3. Her DTW fare changes the order
method.detail: Each total now has 1 LAX + 1 DTW round trip. Europe gets cheaper or shorter for her (Lisbon 11.9h, Naples 11.3h). La Paz needs 2 stops from DTW ($788), and Hong Kong is $1,923 for a 22h itinerary, which pushes both down. For drive trips she flies DTW-LAX ($254 RT, 11.9h with 1 stop; the cheapest is $224 at 19.9h).

Many of the cheapest results were 30-50h itineraries (e.g. Auckland $1,234 at 51h, Hong Kong from DTW $1,190 at 32h). The totals use the cheapest reasonable 1-stop or nonstop fare. HIGH adds $300 for basic-to-standard economy and bags.

Madeira PR trails now need a booked time slot via SIMplifica (EUR 4.50, or EUR 10.50 for PR1; EUR 50 fine without a booking). Taroko (Taiwan) is only partly open (Shakadang closed until about 2031, Zhuilu closed). Samaria Gorge (Crete) is closed in winter (general knowledge, not re-verified).

Jalisco (Puerto Vallarta), Colombia, Guatemala, Israel and Jordan are Level 3. Qatar and UAE are Level 3, so avoid Doha and Dubai connections (affects the Sri Lanka DTW fare). ETIAS for Europe is not live yet. Entry fees added where known: Indonesia about $36 per person, NZ NZ$117-123 per person, Australia ETA AUD 20, Vietnam e-visa $25.

method.item: 7. Points did not affect the ranking
method.detail: The Card & points lines are Credit Max's estimates (from LAX only; award space not checked). Her DTW leg needs its own check. Pay with Sapphire Preferred (no foreign transaction fee).

weights._note: Category shares for the /travel weighted score. They must sum to 1. Changing a share and running `node scripts/travel/build-travel.mjs` re-scores every destination. The page reads the computed totals from trips.json.

weightLegend: Weighted = Outdoors 25% · Food 20% · Museums & City 20% · Price 15% · Getting There 10% · Safety 10%
scoreLegend: Weighted = Outdoors 25% · Food 20% · Museums & City 20% · Price 15% · Getting There 10% · Safety 10%. Weather is pass/fail (all 17 pass), not scored.
safetyHowToRead: Researched Nov 11, 2026 (PT) from Reddit, travel blogs, local news and official park/agency pages. Claims are kept to what the linked sources say. Where a 'safest area' isn't from a source, it's labeled a suggestion. Some Reddit threads could not be opened directly (server error); those claims rely on search-result excerpts. Positions 11-17 were not researched in this depth; they get advisory-based safety scores on the Scores tab.

trips.name: Mexico City
trips.why: Best mix of big hikes and a world-class museum/food city, and the cheapest, easiest meetup for both.
trips.week: Museo Nacional de Antropologia, Frida Kahlo/Coyoacan, Bellas Artes, Teotihuacan. Big hike: La Malinche summit (7.9 mi, 4,320 ft, 14,600 ft altitude; acclimatize, maybe hire a guide, possible ice). Shorter: Tepozteco or Desierto de los Leones. (Ajusco dropped: see Safety tab.) Tacos, mercados, one splurge dinner (Pujol or Contramar).
trips.cardPoints: Pay cash with Sapphire Preferred (CSP); Credit Max's Virgin/Aeromexico award (about $460 in points) doesn't beat the $487 fare.
trips.scoreWhy: Outdoors: one big hike (La Malinche); Ajusco dropped on safety grounds. Food and museums are world-class. Price: $3.5k midpoint. Getting there: 3h45 nonstop for him, 7.8h with 1 stop for her. Safety: Level 2; avoid taxis.

safety.consensus: Widely considered safe for tourists in Roma Norte, Condesa and Polanco, 'on par with other big cities'. The most repeated advice is to never hail street taxis and use Uber or DiDi instead.
safety.risks: 1) Street or airport taxis: overcharging and robbery, and express kidnappings often involve fake or real taxi drivers. Use Uber, DiDi or Cabify (turn on the Uber PIN), or the authorized airport 'sitio' taxis. 2) Phone and jewelry theft, including motorbike snatches in Polanco. Wear no flashy watches or chains. 3) Drinks spiked in bars. Watch your drinks; ATMs only inside banks or malls.
safety.stay: Roma Norte, Condesa, Polanco (Reddit locals). Avoid east of the Zocalo/National Palace at night and north Polanco past the Soumaya.

trips.name: Oaxaca
trips.why: Mexico's best food and crafts city with real mountain hiking. Warmest of the city picks.
trips.week: Museo de las Culturas at Santo Domingo, the Ethnobotanical Garden, Monte Alban, Mitla, Hierve el Agua. Big hike: guided Sierra Norte Cuajimoloyas to Latuvi (10.1 mi, 6.5-7h). Mole, tlayudas, mercado food, mezcal; reserve one dinner (e.g. Criollo or Casa Oaxaca).
trips.advisory: Level 2 (Isthmus region restricted, far from the city)
trips.downsides: Level 2 (Isthmus region restricted, far from the city)
trips.cardPoints: Cash with CSP; the Aeromexico award (about $460) is roughly break-even.
trips.scoreWhy: Outdoors: guided Sierra Norte 10-mile day plus Hierve el Agua. Food: elite. Museums: Santo Domingo museum, Monte Alban; a mid-size city. Getting there: 2 stops for him, 1 stop for her. Safety: Level 2; blockades.

safety.advisory: Level 2 (Oaxaca state; Isthmus restricted for US staff)
safety.consensus: Generally safe for tourists. The real issue is CNTE teacher-union blockades (an inconvenience, not aimed at visitors), not violent crime.
safety.risks: 1) Blockades of streets, toll booths and the airport road: in June 2026 they cut airport access several times, and an Oct 16 strike made some passengers walk about 1 km to the airport. A Section 22 strike that began Nov 4 is ongoing. Check the news and your hotel the morning you fly, leave very early, and never drive through a blockade. 2) Petty theft and ATM crime. Use ATMs inside banks. 3) Mountain driving. Don't drive mountain roads after dark; take a guide or driver.

trips.name: Naples + Amalfi Coast
trips.why: Pompeii, Herculaneum and Naples' museums plus pizza, with Vesuvius and the Path of the Gods. Mild but sometimes wet in January.
trips.week: Naples: National Archaeological Museum, Capodimonte, the Underground. Pompeii and Herculaneum. Hikes: Path of the Gods (Bomerano to Nocelle; real shoes, skip it in rain). Vesuvius is now a guided out-and-back to 1,170 m (the rim loop is closed; book online). Optional: Capri by ferry if seas allow. Pizza at the classics; reserve one dinner.
trips.weather: Naples: high ~56F / low ~40F, about 9 rain days (Naples airport 1991-2020, via Wikipedia)
trips.cardPoints: Maybe: United partner award (about 40k each way to Rome) for his leg.
trips.scoreWhy: Outdoors: Path of the Gods; Vesuvius is now a short guided out-and-back. Food: pizza capital. Museums: MANN, Pompeii, Herculaneum. Getting there: 15h / 11h, 6-9h time shift. Safety: snatch theft.

safety.consensus: Safer than its reputation. Sources and r/napoli say the risks are opportunistic pickpocketing and scooter bag-snatching, not violent crime. The Quartieri Spagnoli are fine by day and on busy streets at night.
safety.risks: 1) Scooter snatches and pickpockets. Carry your bag crossbody on the wall side and don't hold your phone out in narrow lanes. 2) Quiet alleys late at night. Stick to busy streets. 3) Campi Flegrei earthquakes (207 in October 2026) are a background natural hazard west of the city; not a reason to skip.
safety.stay: Chiaia, Vomero, or the historic center along busy streets (suggestion); Sorrento for the Amalfi nights.

trips.name: Andalusia
trips.why: Alhambra, the Seville Alcazar and Picasso museums plus tapas, with gorge and Sierra Nevada foothill hikes. Granada nights get near freezing.
trips.week: Malaga: Picasso Museum, Alcazaba. Caminito del Rey gorge walk (closed Mondays and Jan 11-19, 2027, so book Jan 6-10). Granada: Alhambra (book ahead), Albaicin; a hike in the Alpujarras or the Monachil Los Cahorros gorge. Seville: Alcazar, Cathedral, flamenco. Tapas crawls.
trips.weather: Seville: high ~61F / low ~43F; Granada: ~55F / ~34F (airport normals via Wikipedia)
trips.cardPoints: Maybe: Iberia Avios to Madrid off-peak (about 25.5k each way + $150-200 tax per person; 30% transfer bonus through Dec 1), then train south.
trips.scoreWhy: Outdoors: Caminito del Rey (short, closed Jan 11-19), Los Cahorros, Alpujarras. Food: tapas. Museums: Alhambra, Alcazar, Picasso. Getting there: about 18-19h each. Safety: petty theft only.

safety.consensus: Generally safe. Pickpocketing in crowded tourist spots is the real risk and is rising in Granada (tour guides) and Seville (police union, May 2026).
safety.risks: 1) Pickpockets on Granada's C30/C31 Alhambra buses, at Mirador de San Nicolas and in the Alhambra queues, on Calle Mateos Gago in Seville, and on Calle Larios in Malaga. Bag in front, phone secured. 2) The 'rosemary ladies' and clipboard petition scams. Say no and walk on. 3) Housing and overtourism protests are aimed at policy, not tourists. Give them room.
safety.stay: Seville: Santa Cruz / Arenal; Granada: Realejo or Centro; Malaga: Centro Historico (suggestion; sources give hotspots, not 'safest' lists).

trips.why: Superb food and the National Palace Museum, mild, but Taroko's main gorge trails are closed and the flights are long for her.

trips.name: Lisbon + Sintra / Arrabida
trips.why: Elite museums and food, mild, cheapest Europe flights for both. Hiking is moderate (day hikes, not big mountains).
trips.week: Gulbenkian, Azulejo Museum, MAAT, Belem. Sintra: Pena and the Moorish Castle on foot via Sintra-Cascais park trails; a coastal Arrabida day hike. Pasteis, tascas, seafood; reserve one dinner. Optional 2 nights in Porto.
trips.cardPoints: Maybe: United partner award (about 40k each way) for his leg. Cash is already fairly low.
trips.scoreWhy: Outdoors: moderate day hikes only. Food and museums: excellent. Price: cheapest of Europe. Getting there: 17.7h / 11.9h. Safety: Level 1; pickpockets.

safety.consensus: 'Very safe', including for solo travelers. The one real issue is pickpockets on Tram 28, at viewpoints, in Baixa/Rossio and on the Sintra trains.
safety.risks: 1) Pickpockets working in groups at tram doors. Ride Tram 28 early or late, wear bags in front, and keep nothing in back pockets. 2) Street 'hashish' sellers (fake product). Ignore them. 3) Sintra: car break-ins on forest roads, unlicensed tuk-tuk fares, crowds. Take the train or bus, agree fares first, buy official timed palace tickets.
safety.stay: Central Lisbon is broadly safe. Chiado, Principe Real, Estrela and Campo de Ourique are quieter bases (suggestion). Be alert in crowded Baixa, Rossio and Alfama.

trips.name: Hong Kong
trips.why: Top-tier city food and museums with genuinely great mountain/coastal hiking. Mild and dry. Long-haul, though, and her flight is long and pricey.
trips.week: Hikes: Lantau Peak (sunrise), Dragon's Back, a MacLehose Trail section in Sai Kung. M+ and the Hong Kong Palace Museum, the Peak, Star Ferry. Dim sum, dai pai dong, roast goose; reserve one dinner.
trips.weather: High ~66F / low ~58F, about 6 rain days (Hong Kong Observatory)
trips.dtwFlight: About 22h with 1 stop (United, $1,923). A $1,190 fare takes about 32h.
trips.cardPoints: No award estimate from Credit Max for HK. Pay cash with CSP.
trips.scoreWhy: Outdoors: Lantau Peak, MacLehose, Dragon's Back. Food: elite. Museums: M+, Palace Museum. Price: high because of her $1,923 fare. Getting there: 16h / 22h, 16h shift. Safety: low crime, but national security law and device-password legal risk.

safety.advisory: Level 2 (arbitrary enforcement of local laws / national security laws)
safety.consensus: For ordinary tourists who avoid politics, locals and travelers on Reddit describe visits as uneventful and street crime as very low. The real concern is legal: broadly worded national security laws can apply to foreigners and to online posts.
safety.risks: 1) National security laws: avoid protests or commemorations, don't photograph police or protest scenes, and avoid political posts while there. 2) Devices: since Mar 23, 2026, refusing to give passwords or decryption help in a national-security case is a crime, including in airport transit (State Dept / OSAC). Consider traveling with a minimal phone and data; Reddit travelers discuss wiping phones or using burners. 3) Exit bans and wrongful-detention warnings are aimed at mainland China, not Hong Kong, but don't add a side trip to the mainland without checking.
safety.stay: Tsim Sha Tsui, Central/Sheung Wan, Wan Chai (suggestion; no crime-by-area source).

trips.name: Puerto Rico
trips.why: Cheapest warm trip for both, no passport needed, a real old city plus rainforest hikes. Hikes are shorter than their usual.
trips.week: Old San Juan, El Morro and San Cristobal forts, Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico. El Yunque: El Toro or El Yunque peak trail (reservation for the road). Bioluminescent bay; lechon in Guavate; reserve one dinner in San Juan.
trips.weather: High ~83F / low ~72F, short showers on about 12 days (NOAA)
trips.cardPoints: Pay cash with CSP (fares already low).
trips.scoreWhy: Outdoors: El Yunque hikes are short. Food: good. Museums: Old San Juan forts, art museum. Getting there: about 11-13h with 1 stop each. Safety: car break-ins, outages.

safety.consensus: Tourist areas (Old San Juan, Condado, Isla Verde) are generally safe day and evening. The main risk is theft from rental cars at beaches and trailheads; power outages are a nuisance.
safety.risks: 1) Car break-ins at beach lots and El Yunque trailheads. Leave nothing visible. 2) La Perla and unfamiliar neighborhoods late at night. Avoid them; use Uber or a taxi. 3) Power outages (usually localized, minutes to hours). Book lodging with a generator that covers rooms and AC, and bring a power bank. Rip currents at beaches.
safety.stay: Old San Juan, Condado, Isla Verde

trips.name: Big Island, Hawaii
trips.why: Best pure hiking and nature (active volcano, Mauna Kea, snorkeling); weakest city/museum side.
trips.week: Hawaii Volcanoes NP: Kilauea Iki and Napau Crater (11.9 mi, 5-5.5h). Mauna Kea via the Humu'ula Trail (9-10h, above 12,000 ft) or the stargazing route. Captain Cook / Ka'awaloa hike (1,256 ft) plus snorkeling. Pu'uhonua o Honaunau, the 'Imiloa center in Hilo. Poke, plate lunch; reserve Merriman's Waimea.
trips.cardPoints: Possible saving: BA Avios on Alaska/Hawaiian, about 88k Avios for 2 LAX round trips (Credit Max estimate, about $700 value vs about $894 cash). Her DTW leg needs its own check. Verify on ba.com.
trips.scoreWhy: Outdoors: best in set (volcano park, Mauna Kea). Museums: little city. Price: $5k midpoint. Getting there: 5h50 nonstop / 12.4h. Safety: natural hazards and break-ins.

safety.consensus: Safe for tourists. The risks are nature (volcanic gas and vog, cliff edges, altitude, surf) plus rental-car break-ins at trailheads and beaches.
safety.risks: 1) Car break-ins at trailheads and beach parks. Leave nothing visible and keep valuables with you. 2) Volcanic gas, vog and tephra: NPS warns people with heart or lung conditions. Check the NPS air-quality map and the USGS daily update, and bring a mask and eye protection near active fountaining. 3) Closures: on Oct 7, 2026 the park closed the Halema'uma'u and part of the Byron Ledge trails (seismicity, rockfall). Kilauea is paused after episode 56 (ended Nov 5), and USGS forecast episode 57 for about Nov 16-21.
safety.stay: Kona side for weather (Kailua-Kona, Keauhou, Waikoloa), plus Volcano Village for park access (logistics suggestion, not a sourced safety ranking).

trips.name: Madeira, Portugal
trips.why: The best day-hiking island in Europe, mild all winter, with a pleasant small city in Funchal.
trips.week: PR1 Pico do Arieiro to Pico Ruivo ridge (reopened fully May 2026; booked time slot, EUR 10.50), PR9 Caldeirao Verde levada, Sao Lourenco point, 25 Fontes. Funchal old town, Mercado dos Lavradores, Monte cable car, Madeira wine lodges. Fish (espada), poncha bars.
trips.weather: Funchal: high ~68F / low ~58F, about 6 rain days (Funchal Observatory 1991-2020, via Wikipedia)
trips.cardPoints: Maybe: United partner award (about 40k each way to Lisbon) plus a Lisbon-Funchal hop. Check on United.
trips.scoreWhy: Outdoors: PR1 and levadas, but weather closures happen in winter. Museums: Funchal is small. Getting there: about 22-24h / 17h. Safety: very low crime; trail hazards.

safety.consensus: Very low crime. Trail safety and weather are the issues: winter storms close the whole trail network on warning days, and rockfalls close individual routes.
safety.risks: 1) Weather closures: IFCN closed ALL classified trails on Nov 11, 2026 (IPMA warning, Storm Charles). Keep 2-3 flexible hiking days and check the IFCN list each morning. 2) Rockfall and mud after rain: PR10 is closed (path collapse) and PR16 closed (rockfall). Turn back at fresh rockfall and respect on-site signs even if the online list says open. 3) Falls and rescues: on Nov 6, 2026 a Belgian hiker broke a leg on PR1 and bad weather stopped the helicopter, so ground teams carried her out.
safety.stay: Funchal (Zona Velha / Lido) is the usual base (suggestion; no area-crime data found).

trips.name: Tenerife, Canary Islands
trips.why: Warmest place in Europe, with big volcano hikes. Small-city culture only (La Laguna).
trips.week: Teide: summit by permit (or Montana Blanca trail plus the cable car), the Roques de Garcia loop. Anaga forest ridges; Masca gorge (booking required, check status). La Laguna old town, Museo de la Naturaleza y Arqueologia. Guachinches (local wine taverns).
trips.cardPoints: Maybe: Iberia Avios via Madrid (Iberia flies to the Canaries).
trips.scoreWhy: Outdoors: Teide (permit), Anaga, Masca. Museums: La Laguna only. Getting there: 18h / 21h. Safety: peaceful protests; hiking rescues.

safety.consensus: Safe and still welcoming. The 2026 overtourism and housing protests are peaceful, mostly in Santa Cruz and aimed at governments and landlords. Theft from rental cars is the bigger everyday risk.
safety.risks: 1) Rental-car and beach theft. Use secure parking and leave nothing visible. 2) Timeshare 'winning scratch card' scams on seafronts. Walk away. 3) Protests and strikes (Spain-wide general strike Nov 11, 2026). Not relevant for January, but check the news.
safety.stay: Puerto de la Cruz (2025 crime down 13.56%, El Dia) or Costa Adeje.
